title: Two sessions dispatch onto one branch: add a branch-ownership guard

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Two sessions dispatched writers onto one branch three times tonight. The result was lost work, rejected pushes and a near force-push. The process needs an ownership guard.

## The cases

- #3567: an `issue-worker-max` held the claim from 22:14Z. A second worker (`issue-worker-high`) claimed again at 22:29Z and later pushed `e7ae538a3` to the same branch while the max worker had its own commit. The max worker's work was lost with its worktree.
- #3650: our rework worker (local `62809f42f`, on merge `68c10fc24`) and another session's implementation (`bfefff3bd` -> merge `5711344b0` -> `864897476`) diverged on `issue/2970-rotary-parallel-band`. The push would have been rejected or would have clobbered. The local design is held and recorded on the PR.
- #3577: a max-tier rework and a text-fix worker both wrote `issue/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end`; the text fix pushed `4d464e006` over the rework's head while the rework's independent duplicate stayed uncommitted.
- Same class, earlier: prepared branches were pushed by the coordinating session while the worker that made them was about to push (`#3391`, `#3494`).

## Harm

- A worker spends an hour, then cannot push.
- A push race invites a force-push, which the law forbids.
- Two reviews run on two implementations of one fix.
- The status reports disagree, and the coordinator relays a head that is not ours (as happened with #3650).

## Rule

Whoever claims the issue owns the branch. One writer for one branch at one time. A second session that finds a live claim or a live writer on the branch stands down and names the live writer.

## What to change

- A branch owner record that both sessions read before a dispatch: a claim comment on the PR (or the issue) that names the writer and the base, or a small `.claude/claims/issue-N` file with the writer, the branch and the head it started from.
- The coordinator checks the PR head and the owner record before every dispatch, and writes its own record.
- A push that the remote refuses because the branch moved is a STOP with a report, never a force-push.
- The skills that dispatch (`work-issue`, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `merge-ready`) say where the record lives.

## Related

- #3567, #3577, #3650.
- The two-session setup itself: a second session and this coordinator both write the same repository.

body:
Found in the second safety read of PR #3166 (#1874). None of these can give a wrong scale: a file with no length unit is never imported until the unit is stated.

1. **A second question replaces the first.** `crates/ui/src/state_step_units.rs:28-31` and `state.rs` (about line 4522): drop two STEP files with no unit at the same time. The second refusal writes over `step_units_ask`. The question for the first file is lost with no message on the status line, and that file is not imported. **Wanted:** a queue, or a status line that names each file that waits.
2. **The browser has no prompt.** `crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs:203`: the import from bytes (the browser file picker) calls `from_bytes` with no unit and an empty `import_file`. The user gets "import refused: ... state the unit ..." and cannot state it. **Wanted:** the same prompt for the bytes path.
3. **A fixture binding can go to the wrong file.** `state_step_units.rs:41`: while an import runs, `resolve_step_units` sets `import_as_fixture` again, and the running import of a different file can take it. The same race is on `main` in the import-as-fixture flow; the prompt adds a second way into it.
4. **A file with no unit is read two times:** one full read that ends with the refusal, then the read with the unit. A large file pays the read cost twice. **Wanted:** find the missing unit before the full read.
5. The kernel functions `read_step`, `import_step` and `import_step_model` with no unit still read a file with no unit as mm. Only kernel tests call them; the geometry layer refuses. Make them refuse too, or make them private to tests.
6. No `layout_window_step_units_prompt` test exists (the DXF units dialog and the overwrite prompt have none either).

body:
Found in the delta read of PR #3650 (#2970). None of these can cause a wrong program.

1. **Cost.** `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/gaps.rs` (about lines 85-185): the check uses a fixed grid of 48 x 72 rays, but each ray reads each facet near its station with no search structure. On a mesh with hundreds of thousands of facets this can add seconds to each generate. Add a bucket by station and angle, or reuse the support grid.
2. **Units.** The note gives the stations in mm in an inch document too. Use the document unit.
3. **Frame.** The stations are in the local x of the laid frame, and the angle is "from the top of the laid bar toward its +y side". A user cannot see that frame. Use the setup axis and a direction that the viewport shows, or the rotary angle word of the machine.
4. **Picked faces.** With picked faces the note can say "all the way round" when only the picked faces are cut.
5. **Chord samples.** `gaps.rs:41` caps the samples along one chord at 4096. A very long straight pass at a very fine step can get samples wider than the cover distance. The result is one extra clear cut or a false "no pass reaches" note, never a lost cut. Scale the cap with the chord length.
6. The pin `a_keyway_is_cut_once_in_each_place` uses 0.1 mm; the filter's own "same place" distance is half a pass spacing. Make the pin use the filter's distance.

body:
What happens:
Since the fix for #2970, Rotary Parallel cuts the full turn of the bar when Bottom is at the underside of the bar. A machine with limited rotary travel cannot always turn the tool to the underside. An example is `tilthead.mch`, with B -120..120. On that machine, the machine check refuses the full-turn program and names the axis, the angle and the travel. Nothing posts.

The workaround today: set Bottom above the axis. The cut then stays on the upper arc, symmetric about the top. The user cannot state a different arc, for example 0..240 degrees, or an arc that is not symmetric.

Expected:
- Rotary Parallel has an operation parameter for the angular range: full turn (the default) or a stated arc (start and end angle about the fitted axis).
- With a stated arc, the passes stay on that arc.
- A note names the arc that is not cut.
- Undo and redo go through `EditOperationParams`. The MCP tool gets the field.

Evidence:
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/halves.rs` (the two halves, #2970).
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs`: `a_full_turn_rotary_parallel_refuses_on_a_head_that_cannot_reach_under`.

Found while fixing #2970. A strategy fork is an operation parameter with a default.

Done means: a Rotary Parallel with a stated arc posts clean on `tilthead.mch` within its B travel, and the path note names the uncut arc.

## What to build

Add the pure domain model and compatibility checks for reusable tool components in `crates/tools`.

1. Add `ToolComponent` with three ISO 13399 kinds:
   - `CuttingItem`: an indexable insert (`InsertSpec`) or a parametric solid `Tool`.
   - `ToolItem`: a turning holder, boring bar body, or indexable cutter body with one `MCS` and one or more `CSW*` insert seats (`InsertSeatSpec`).

2. Add normalized ISO/TS 13399-60 `ConnectionCode` types for `ADINTMS` and `ADINTWS` (steep tapers, HSK, PSC/ISO 26623, KM/ISO 26622, ER/ISO 15488, Weldon/DIN 1835-B, cylindrical shank, TTS, ISO 5608 rectangular shank, VDI, BMT, shell-mill arbor, and custom string).
3. Add ISO 1832 insert designation parsing (positions 1 to 7: shape, clearance, tolerance, fixing, size/IC, thickness, nose radius) and ISO 5608 seat parameters (clamping, shape, approach angle, clearance, hand, size).
4. Add pure compatibility checks (`check_insert_fit`, `check_coupling_fit`) and library query helpers (`compatible_parents`, `compatible_children`).
5. Refuse every mismatch by name. Each refusal states both component names, the mismatched property, the expected value, and the actual value.

## Clean-room provenance

Use only public standards (`ISO 13399`, `ISO 1832`, `ISO 5608`, `ISO 15488`, `ISO 26622`, `ISO 26623`, `ISO 12164`, `ISO 10889`, `JIS B 6339`, `ASME B5.50`, `DIN 1835`) and existing code in `crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs`.

- Unit tests in `crates/tools` pin ISO 1832 code parsing for common turning and milling inserts.
- Unit tests pin valid insert-to-holder and coupling matches, plus `compatible_parents` ("holders that take this insert") and `compatible_children` queries.
- Unit tests pin named refusals for wrong shape, wrong clearance, wrong size/IC, wrong thickness, wrong clamping/fixing, wrong hand, and wrong coupling code.

Research in #2593 selected a file contract for URDF machine models (for example, exports from SolidCraft). The `.mch` file names the URDF file and maps each `.mch` axis letter to one URDF joint. Existing `.mch` files without `urdf` keep reading unchanged.

title: 3D Finish links: check if a hop with a retract height below the end of the run feeds the tool down into the part

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
Found in the review read of PR #3625 (#3362). **This is a hypothesis from a read of the code. No test or run shows it yet. The first step is a test.** The priority is `P1` because the possible result is a gouge that passes; correct the priority when the test gives the answer.

## What the read found

`emit_runs` in `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/march.rs` (about lines 347-390 on `main` at `7c637d705`), the plain hop between two runs (about lines 381-383): the travel height is `trav = hop.max(z0)`, where `hop` is the retract height and `z0` is the Z of the start of the next run. The Z of the end of the current run (`cur.z`) is not in the formula. The hop is not checked against the model.

If the run that ends is higher than the start of the next run, and the retract height is below `cur.z`, the tool moves down at the current XY to `trav`, and then makes a rapid across at that height. At the current XY the tool is on the surface. A move down from there goes into the part.

## Where it can occur

- On `main` today: a cavity with the Contour or Flat pattern (the outer pass is high, the inner pass is low), when the retract height of the operation is below the high pass.
- With PR #3625 and `Pass starts at: Inside`: a convex part (a dome), because the inner pass is high and the next pass is lower.
- With a retract height above the top of the part (the usual setup) the fault cannot occur: `hop` is then above `cur.z`.

## Not known

1. Whether a rule refuses a retract height below the top of the part when the operation is made or edited.
2. Whether the verifier gives a blocking finding for the move down and for the rapid across.

## Wanted

1. A test, first: a cavity fixture on `main` with Contour, a retract height between the two passes, and the verifier. Read the moves of the hop, and the findings.
2. If the tool goes into the part: `trav` must not be below `cur.z` (for example `hop.max(z0).max(cur.z)`), and the rapid across must be checked like the other links (`diagonal_ok` / `straight_ok`) or go to the clearance height. Pin it for a cavity and for a dome.
3. If a rule already refuses that retract height, or the verifier blocks the post: say so here, pin that fact, and set the priority to `P3` or close the issue with the pin.

The decision file of PR #3625 says that each link "is certified by the existing laws". Correct that sentence for the plain hop when the answer is known.

title: The verifier slices at every cut Z: an interpolated ramp turns 3 planes into 1,700 and minutes into hours

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Waiting on another issue or a decision

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The verifier slices the part at every distinct cut Z. A path with an interpolated ramp has about 1,700 cut planes instead of the 3 cut levels, and the band-reach and tangency laws then take minutes. The same path takes 89.6 s as a whole suite on main.

## Evidence

From PR #3577's head (one Waterline Outside generation, debug, temporary counters, reverted):

- The generator is fast: `ring_plan_ramped` 110 ms; each level walk 1.5 to 1.8 ms; 186 `dead_end_ramp`/`push_zig` calls are all in microseconds.
- The path is 8,850 moves and 8,553 feed moves, with 1,697 distinct feed-move Z values (the cut levels are 3: z = 12, 2, 1.5).
- The time is in the verify laws:
  - `section::tangency` 28.3 s;
  - `section::solid` 0.82 s;
  - `band_reach` plane sections and grid 1.4 s, with 5,596,906 boundary samples at a 2.75 mm cell;
  - `band_reach` verdict loop: moves 0 to 6000 in 55 ms (all skipped by the `h0 >= stock_top_z` guard), then more than 148 s without finishing for the remaining 2,850 moves; single moves take 2.8 s and 28 s, about 150k `sample_tests` per move.

The unmodified single test was killed at 120 s: 100 percent CPU, 0.1 s system time, 471 MB RSS. It is CPU-bound.

## Cause

The new dead-end entry posts a zig-zag ramp, one feed move per thinned vertex per lap (`crates/motion/src/links.rs`, `push_zig`). `Rest::new` (`crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs:89-100`) records one cut per feed chord, keyed on `m.to.z`. The path therefore has about 1,700 distinct cut planes. `band_reach_counted` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:47`, the plane loop at 102-110 and the verdict loop near 205-240) slices the part at every distinct cut Z, so the work is `O(feed_moves x samples)`, and samples grow with the plane count: quadratic in the number of ramp Z steps. `section::tangency` (`crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:89-146`) pays the same per-distinct-Z cost through `rest.islands_at`.

The new planner code is ruled out: `level_order.rs`, `level_rings.rs` (`order`, `unswept`, `too_short_at`), `level_ramp_entry.rs`, `descent.rs::ramp_fallback`, `links.rs::plan_zig_capped/push_zig` and the `arc_cross` retries are all sub-millisecond to about 100 ms.

## Recommended fix

In `band_reach_counted`, build the sampled plane set from the cut LEVELS (feed moves with `|from.z - to.z| < z_tol`) plus the deepest cut, instead of every `rest.cut()` record, and pass that set to the same `islands_at` and `boundary_samples` code. For this path that is 3 to 4 planes and restores the pre-PR cost; the same plane set also removes the 28 s in `section::tangency`.

This slightly reduces wall-sample coverage for ramps between levels. The heavy lanes on a sloped or stepped fixture must show that the verdicts do not change before it merges. A lower-risk variant is to quantize the plane key and cap the sample count.

## Why #3595 did not cover it

#3595 (`9a7de3781`) made the sample lookup exact and fast. It did not reduce the number of planes, so the per-plane cost stays.

## Related

- #3577: the ramp entry that exposes this; blocked until this is fixed.
- #3588: the verifier speed work, closed by #3595.
- #3587: the slow pin as a test-speed item.

title: Stock preview: a ray that uses all its march steps is discarded, so the cut stock shows holes that change with the view

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A user reported this in chat on 2026-11-22.

## What happens

In the simulation, the traced stock picture shows holes in the stock. Through a hole, the user sees the viewport grid behind the stock. The holes are on the faced floor, near the tool path. When the user orbits the camera, the holes change shape. Thus the cause is in the picture, not in the stock data.

The user saw this in a local build. The exact version is not known.

## Expected

The picture shows the stock as solid where the stock has material. A pixel that the march cannot resolve does not show the background as if the stock were cut through.

## Cause (from a read of `origin/main` f35202134, not built)

- `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` gives each ray `MAX_STEPS = 64` steps. Each step is `phi * RELAX` (0.9).
- Near a large flat face, at a low view angle, `phi` is small. The steps become small, and the ray uses all 64 steps before a hit. The ray returns status 2 (unreadable).
- `crates/ui/src/trace/composite.wgsl` (lines 47-50) discards each pixel that is not a resolved hit. The traced picture replaces the stock slot, so nothing is drawn behind the pixel. The user sees the background.
- The comment there says that a budget bail is "never painted as material". That rule is correct. But a hole also gives a wrong picture: the stock looks cut through.

## Not affected

The Deviate verdict, the post gate and the STL export do not read the traced picture. The G-code is not affected.

## Possible fixes

1. Paint a budget bail at the last march point, with a tint that shows that it is approximate. Do not discard it.
2. Increase the step budget, or set a minimum step near a surface (for example a fraction of the cell).
3. Keep the CPU twin (`camcraft_sim::stock_sim::preview::march`) in parity. The parity test is `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.

## Related

- #3336: stock simulation performance.
- The `machined.rs` mesh is not shown when the GPU eye traces. A separate change can show the mesh when the transport is down.

Done means: a grazing view of a faced stock floor shows no background pixels inside the stock outline. A test pins this on the CPU twin, and the GPU parity test stays green.

title: No way to open a project read-only: Save can write over a reference copy

labels.name: enhancement

body:
**What happened**

CamCraft cannot open a project read-only. Every open project saves over its own file:

- In the window, Save writes to the file that was opened (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3436-3440` on `main` 60b19abe8).
- The MCP tool `save_project` without a path, and the script call `cam.save()`, write to the file that was opened (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41-52`).
- `camcraft-ui` has no read-only option. `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` stops with `unknown option '--read-only'` (`crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs:192`).
- The MCP tool `open_project` takes only `path`. `open_project {"path": "job.camproj", "read_only": true}` is refused with `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:115-123`).

These users need a project that opens without a risk to its file:

- a user who opens a shipped example or a tester kit to look at it;
- a person who reviews a released job;
- a team that keeps reference copies on a shared folder.

CamCraft already has this behaviour for shipped machines. The machine editor refuses Save for a shipped machine, and Save As writes a copy (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:35-36`, `:229-242`, `:259`).

**Expected**

- `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only.
- A save over the opened file is refused on every save route: the window, MCP `save_project` and script `cam.save`. The file stays byte for byte.
- Save As to another file works, and the project is then no longer read-only.
- The title bar says that the project is read-only.
- An agent can open a project read-only with `open_project {"path": ..., "read_only": true}`.

An open SolidCraft pull request adds the same option, `solidcraft --read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830). The same name and behaviour in both apps help users who use the two.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Copy a project file, for example a shipped example, to a folder.
2. Run `camcraft-ui --read-only <copy>.camproj`. The start stops with `unknown option '--read-only'`.
3. Run `camcraft-ui <copy>.camproj`. Change a parameter and push Save. CamCraft writes over the copy.
4. In `camcraft-cli mcp`, call `open_project {"path": "<copy>.camproj", "read_only": true}`. The call is refused: `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"`.

I found this by code inspection.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at 60b19abe8 (2026-11-22). Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- A new start option `--read-only` in the option table (`cli_options.rs`). It applies to the one project file on the command line. A model file is imported as usual, because an import makes a new project with no file. A headless start ignores it.
- One rule in `crates/app/src/project/`, `project::refuse_read_only_save`, next to `project::save` and its other refusals. It refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The window's `save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it. `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP seam of a window.
- The rule compares files, not spellings (canonical paths), because the Save As dialog gives an absolute path.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as the shipped-machine editor does. A save to the opened file from the dialog is refused on the status line.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- MCP `open_project` gets an optional `read_only` boolean. Scripts get it through `cam.call("open_project", ...)`. The live seam still refuses `open_project`, but the window's read-only state reaches a live `save_project`.
- The title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.
- No file-format change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.

**Done means:** `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only and the title says so. Tests show that a save over the opened file is refused, and that the file stays byte for byte, through the window, MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live seam. Tests show that a save to another file works and ends read-only. A test shows that the option parses and keeps the file argument. The help text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`, the site guide and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` describe it.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Project save writes over a `.camproj` that changed on disk, with no warning: the other changes are lost

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happened**

A save replaces a newer project file on disk with no warning, and the other changes are lost.

When the `.camproj` file on disk changed after CamCraft opened or saved it, the next save to that file writes over it. The save does not check the file first, and no message shows. The work that the other window, program or person saved is gone.

Nothing records the file's state when a project is opened or saved:

- The window: `State::save_project_path` (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:4722`) calls `project::save` directly. `State::open_project_path` (`state.rs:4669`) reads the file and keeps only its path.
- The script call `cam.save` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41`) and the MCP tool `save_project` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:152`) do the same. Without a path, `save_project` "saves over the file last opened or saved".
- The only file-stamp checks in the UI are for linked models and theme files (`crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs:94`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files.rs:130`).

This can occur when:

- the same project is open in two CamCraft windows;
- a `git pull` or a branch switch changes the file while CamCraft is open;
- a colleague saves the same file in a shared folder;
- a sync client (OneDrive, Dropbox) replaces the file with a version from another computer.

**Expected**

Before a save replaces the project's own file, CamCraft checks that the file did not change since it was opened or last saved. If it changed:

- the window asks before it writes (overwrite, save as another file, or cancel);
- a script or an agent gets a refusal that names the file, and can give an explicit overwrite option.

SolidCraft has the same behaviour: its `file.save` refuses such a file unless `overwrite` is set.

**Steps to reproduce**

I found this by code inspection. I did not run these steps on a machine.

1. Open `job.camproj` in two CamCraft windows, A and B.
2. In B, add an operation and save.
3. In A, make a different change and save.
4. Open `job.camproj` again: the operation from B is gone. No window showed a message.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at `60b19abe8` (2026-11-22). The same code is in v0.25.0. Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- Remember a disk stamp of the project file (path, size, modification time) at open and after each save. It reads no file content, so a large project costs the same as a small one.
- Before a save to that file, take the stamp again. If it is different:
  - the window shows a prompt: **Save As**, **Cancel**, **Overwrite**. Nothing is written before the answer;
  - `cam.save` and `save_project` refuse by name. `save_project` gets an optional `overwrite` argument, and `cam.save` gets an options object `{ overwrite }`.
- A save to another path, a new document, and a file that was deleted are not checked.
- An agent attached to the window uses the window's stamp, so its save is checked too, and the window does not ask about the agent's own save.
- `project::save` and the file format do not change.

**Done means:** when the project's own file on disk changed after the open or the last save, a save to it is held in the window and refused for scripts and MCP. `overwrite: true` (or Overwrite in the window) replaces the file. Tests show the refusal, the overwrite option, and that a save directly after our own save is not refused.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

body:
On one Windows machine the build step of `cargo xtask gate quick --base main` failed in 4 of 4 runs with the default job budget (16). It passed in 4 of 4 runs with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`. The source did not change between the runs. This is a different fault from #3589 (the crash of the lib test process).

## What happens
Step 1 of the quick plan is `ui build (--no-run)`. Its command is:

    cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-ui --no-run --lib --test boundary --test boundary_picks --test contour_dxf_sketch --test sinker_setup --test tap_hand --test theme_example --test theme_files --test waterjet_tool

It fails with "compile error". The first error of each failing run names a dependency crate, and it is a different crate each time:

    error[E0460]: found possibly newer version of crate `png` which `camcraft_app` depends on
    error[E0462]: found staticlib `zerocopy` instead of rlib or dylib which `camcraft_app` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `accesskit` which `camcraft_ui` depends on
    error[E0786]: found invalid metadata files for crate `test`

Each run then shows many errors of the form `error[E0463]: can't find crate for 'camcraft_ui'` (or `camcraft_app`). Those follow from the first error. The 8 integration suites after the failed build still ran and passed in each run.

## Conditions

title: Verifier: the tangency law slices the model one time for each distinct Z (34.7 s on a ramp entry)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the work on #3588 (PR for `band_reach`). Refs #3567, #3577.

## What happens
The tangency law (b), `section::tangency` in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` (about lines 74-147), takes one island slice for each move. The slice is at `min(from.z, to.z) + lift` (`section.rs:96`), through `Rest::islands_at`. The island cache (`rest.rs:146-157`) keys on the exact bits of Z. A ramp entry has a different Z at each move, so each move pays one full slice of the model.

Measured by the worker of #3567 in debug, on `pocket_pass_start::fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` with PR #3577: tangency takes 34.7 s for 2232 moves that are not planar (about 15 ms for each slice). Planning takes 0.21 s.

#3588 fixes the cost of `band_reach` only. `band_reach` uses the same slices; for a flat cutter (`lift` 0) on a descending ramp they are the same cache keys, so the slice cost is paid one time, in tangency.

## Why this needs its own design
The slice itself is the cost, not the use of it. Each plane gives a different Region: a face of two triangles crosses each plane at a different point. A reuse of one slice for a Z interval, or a snap of the key, changes the section that the law judges. That is a change of a gouge check, under the safety floor.

Possible directions (not decided):
- Slice incrementally: sort the facets by Z span, and keep the active set between two planes.
- Prove that two planes with no facet vertex between them give the same verdict for the law, and reuse the slice for them.
- Measure the release build first: if it is seconds there, lower the priority.

## Done means
- A path with about 2000 distinct cut Z values verifies tangency in a time that does not grow with moves x slice cost, or the release time is measured and found small.
- The findings of the tangency law do not change on the existing tests (an equivalence test against the old law).

### Context
- On `#1958` (2026-11-19), the machine owner reported that an AC trunnion mounts at different positions on the mill table across jobs, so its `A` pivot location in MCS must be configurable in the setup rather than fixed in one `.mch` file.
- `#1962` stores `A.pivot` only in `.mch`, and `#1970` adds `.mch` trunnion editing plus setup `wcs_offset` (part WCS relative to `C` platter).
- In `crates/post/src/kinematics/math.rs` (lines 265-268), `P_mach = a_pivot + R_A(phi_a) * (c_offset + R_C(phi_c) * (tip + wcs_offset))` and `xyz_G54 = P_mach - work_datum`. Moving the trunnion on the table changes `a_pivot`, which affects linear stroke checks (`#1969`), table collision sweeps (`#1973`), and `G54` coordinates when `work_datum` is fixed on the table.
- `SetupDef::nose_to_axis` (`crates/app/src/schema.rs` lines 322-345, `crates/app/src/rotary_stack.rs`) sets the precedent for a setup-level override of a machine rotary figure.

### Requirements
- Add optional `trunnion_pivot: Option<[f64; 3]>` (MCS mm) and an explicit work-datum reference mode (`C` platter center at `A = 0, C = 0`, `A` pivot, part WCS at `A = 0, C = 0`, or explicit MCS `G54` vector) to `SetupDef` in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`.
- Add undoable command(s), MCP tool(s) (per AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"), and project file serialization (with `PROJECT_VERSION` bump if breaking).
- Expose the setup trunnion pivot and work-datum mode controls in the Setup UI alongside `#1970`'s WCS-to-pivot offset.
- Resolve effective `a_pivot` as `setup.trunnion_pivot.or(machine_a.pivot)` and stream effective `a_pivot`, `wcs_offset`, and `work_datum` into `.cnc` `PARAM`s for both `machine::check_ops` (`#1969`) and `post::engine`.
- Refuse non-RTCP multi-axis posting by name when neither the setup nor the `.mch` file states a valid finite `A` pivot.

Done means: Users can set or clear a per-setup trunnion `A` pivot position and work-datum reference in GUI and MCP, undo/redo and save/reload it, stream it to the post and machine checker, and get a named refusal when non-RTCP 5-axis posting lacks a stated pivot.

body:
The `camcraft-ui` lib test binary often ends with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (0xc0000005) on Windows. The crash is in the test process, not in one test. It makes `cargo xtask gate quick` red at the step `ui suites: lib` about half of the time.

## What happens
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` runs. The process stops with `process didn't exit successfully ... (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)`.
- No test shows FAILED. There is no panic message and no summary line. The last lines are `... ok` lines of different tests.
- The crash comes after 332 to 381 tests have finished (of 1479). The last test is different each time. Examples: `egui_app::tests::a_gated_dropdown_row_click_answers_and_closes`, `egui_app::status_alert::tests::ordinary_status_is_not_an_alert`, `egui_app::start_exit_rows::tests::a_typed_start_point_applies_through_the_history_and_undoes`, `egui_app::sinker_pass_tests::a_rough_op_shows_its_pass_and_the_finished_cavity_size`.

## How often
Debug profile (`cargo test`, unoptimized + debuginfo), default number of test threads (16):
- Plain `main` (commit 4c0a157e1): 8 of 15 runs crashed. The tests finished before the crash: 332, 354, 358, 361, 362, 369, 371, 371.
- A branch with a small, unrelated change (a worker thread for the stock eye): 2 of 10 runs crashed, after 366 and 381 tests.

## Conditions
- It is not tied to the job count of the gate. `cargo xtask gate quick` crashed with 16 jobs (`--test-threads=16`). It crashed once with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` (`--test-threads=4`) and passed once with 4 jobs on a different branch.
- One test thread: 6 of 6 runs passed (1475 tests, about 3 minutes each, `main`). So the crash needs tests that run at the same time. This is a reading of 6 runs, not a proof.
- Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, a laptop with 16 logical CPUs.
- GPU: Intel Arc B390 (integrated), driver 32.0.101.8628.
- Toolchain: rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13), cargo 1.99.1, target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.

## Effect on the gate
- `ui suites: lib` is red in about half of the runs. A change that does not touch the cause cannot show a green lib step reliably.
- A pull request that needs the quick gate can show 1479 passed in one run and a crash in the next run on the same head.

## Stack trace
There is none. I tried for about one hour and did not change any CamCraft code.
- No debugger is installed here. Windows crash dumps need a registry change with administrator rights. I did not make it.
- I wrote a small program that starts the test binary with the Win32 debug API and prints the stacks of all threads at the first access violation. With the debugger attached, the test process ended on its own with exit code 0 or 101 after 70 to 119 tests, in every run, so it could not reproduce the crash. I think a debugger changes what the process does. I did not find why.

## Questions for the maintainers
1. Does the crash happen on your runner (`post-merge.yml`, Windows or other)? Do you know the cause?
2. While it exists, how do you want a pull request treated if `ui suites: lib` crashes but the pinning tests, run by name, pass? My plan is to name the crash in the PR body and to show the named tests.
3. Which setting should I use to get a crash dump (for example `LocalDumps` for `camcraft_ui-*.exe`), if you want one?

## A different observation, probably not related
With 16 jobs, the step `ui build (--no-run)` of `cargo xtask gate quick` failed in 4 of 4 runs with `found invalid metadata files` or `found possibly newer version of crate`. The crate was `png`, `accesskit`, `zerocopy` and `test` in different runs. `cargo clean -p camcraft-ui` did not help. With `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` the build step passed in both runs. I think it is a build-cache problem on this machine. I did not look further.

title: Verifier: band_reach takes minutes when a toolpath has many cut planes (a ramp entry)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2

labels.name: area:sim

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the work on #3567 (PR #3577, the ramp entry at a dead end).

## What happens
The verifier `camcraft_sim::verify::verify_bodies` takes minutes for a 2D toolpath that goes down by ramps. Measured in debug on the test `pocket_pass_start::fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`:

| Tree | Time |
|---|---|
| `main` (4c0a157e1) | 89.6 s, pass |
| PR #3577 at e7ae538a3 | more than 1500 s (stopped) |
| the same with the ramp thinned to the arc-fit tolerance | more than 9 minutes (stopped) |

The planning and the emit of the path take 0.21 s (8850 moves, 33 passes). The time is in the verifier:
- crossings: 0.0 s;
- tangency: 34.7 s for 2232 moves that are not planar;
- solid: 1 s;
- `reach::band_reach` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:72-80`): not complete after 3 minutes.

## Cause
Each ramp move ends at its own Z. `band_reach` slices the model at each different cut Z (`rest.islands_at`), adds the boundary samples of each slice to one sample set, and tests each move against the whole set. The cost is about moves x planes x samples. A path with helices, as on `main`, has few planes. The tangency check slices one time for each different Z also (about 15 ms each in debug).

The same cost can come from any path with many different Z values: a ramp entry that a user selects today, a helix with a small pitch, a 3D path. A user waits minutes with no progress and no message. The Prime Directive asks for a clean result, not a hang.

## Wanted
- `band_reach` keeps the island samples for each plane and tests a move only against the planes that it reaches (or an index by Z), so that the cost does not grow with moves x planes.
- The cache key of `islands_at` and the tangency slices are checked for the same pattern.
- A test with a ramp of many small moves pins a time or a count bound (a count of slice calls is better than wall time).
- The findings of the verifier do not change: pin them on the existing cases (this is a collision and gouge check, under the safety floor).

## Why P2
PR #3577 (the fix of #3567) cannot merge before this: with it, a 2D Offset or 2D Pocket with Pass starts at Outside takes minutes to verify. Measure the release build also and correct the priority if it is seconds there.

## Cause (found in the code)
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_window.rs` (`init_gpu`) creates the window with default attributes. In winit 0.30.13 a visible, active window is shown with `ShowWindow(SW_SHOW)` (`window_state.rs`, `apply_diff`).
- The same function then calls `window.focus_window()`. On Windows this sends a synthetic Alt key press to get past the foreground lock, so the lock timeout does not matter.
- Nothing in the program reads the launcher's show state.

## Proposal
Two new start options in the `cli_options` table:
- `--no-activate`: create the window inactive and do not call `focus_window()`. The window shows, and the focused window keeps the focus.
- `--minimized`: the same, and the window starts minimized. It covers no other window.

The default does not change. A separate step could read STARTUPINFO on Windows. That is a larger change, so it is not proposed here.

A patch is ready on a branch. It has unit tests for the parser and the window attributes. I also checked both options with the project on the command line, from a process started by Task Scheduler (not from a terminal). The window was never the foreground window, and it did not take the focus when the project finished loading. `--minimized` gave a minimized window. Not tested: macOS, Linux.

Is this the wanted shape?

Found by reading, in the second read of PR #3502. It is not a fault of that PR: the code is on `main`. **Nothing was run. This is a hypothesis.** The first step is a test that proves or disproves it.

## The hypothesis
The hole recognizers `recognize` and `recognize_cross` (`crates/motion/src/drilling/recognize.rs:87,97`) classify a hole from its wall facets with `WALL_NZ 0.7` and a circle fit with `FIT_TOL 0.02` (`recognize.rs:39,44`), in the setup frame.

A hole whose axis is tilted 2 degrees from the tool axis has a section that differs from a true circle by about 0.0006 r. That is far below the fit tolerance. Such a hole can pass as a Z hole. The drilling operation then drills along Z, and the drill cuts into the wall of the real hole. This is a gouge that passes with no message.

## Why P1
If the hypothesis is true, the posted program cuts in the wrong place and nothing blocks the post (the table: "a gouge or collision that passes").

## Wanted
1. A test with a part that has one hole tilted 2 degrees and one tilted 5 degrees from the tool axis (made from code, no model file). Assert what detection gives for each: a Z hole, a skipped hole with a name, or a cross hole.
2. If a tilted hole is taken as a Z hole: a tolerance on the angle of the axis (small, for example the angle at which the drill moves the wall by more than the tolerance of the operation over the hole depth), and a named skip for a hole outside it. Record the tolerance as a decision. Consider a parameter with a default (CAM choices are user parameters).
3. If the test shows that detection already refuses or skips the tilted hole: keep the test as a pin and close this issue with the commit.

## What to do

Add one internal shape type in `camcraft-tools`: the tool meridian. It is the cutting outline `rho(z)`, tip up, made of lines and circular arcs. All consumers read the tool shape through it in later sub-issues.

1. A new module (for example `crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`, under 400 lines). It holds the meridian type and `Tool::meridian()`. Reuse the point form of `SpunProfile` (`crates/tools/src/spun.rs`: `z`, `r`, signed `arc`).
2. `Tool::meridian()` gives the meridian of each existing mill kind from its numbers: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Taper`, `Drill`, and the undercut heads of #1444 (`Lollipop`, `Dovetail`, `TSlot`, `Keyseat`). It agrees with `Tool::profile` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:387-465`) on the cutting band.
3. A split of the meridian into convex atoms:
   - a straight segment gives a frustum (each slope);
   - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
   - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (outer bound) or tangent frusta (inner bound), with a sag limit as a parameter.
4. Each atom carries a flag: cutting, or non-cutting (a pilot bearing band).
5. Degenerate input (a zero-length segment, a negative radius, a non-finite value, an arc that does not fit its chord) gives a named error. It never panics.

No consumer changes in this issue. No toolpath, simulation or check changes.

## Rules

- The geometry is from elementary plane geometry (chord sag `R (1 - cos(theta / 2))`) and convexity (Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, 3.2.5). Each module has its provenance line. No HSMWorks material.
- `effort:max`: a new geometry algorithm and the shape law that the gouge checks will read.

## Done means

- `Tool::meridian()` exists for each mill kind listed above.
- Tests pin, for each existing kind, that its convex atoms are the same solids that `Cutter::atoms` (`crates/sim/src/verify/probe.rs:180-230`) builds today, within 1e-9 mm.
- Tests pin the outer and inner bounds of a concave arc: the outer union contains the arc, the inner union stays inside it, and each sag is under the limit.
- Tests pin a named error for each degenerate input.

body:
Implement the core 4-axis cylindrical flow-line toolpath kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`.

What to build:
- Accept picked 3D guide edge chains, part facets, a rotary `Axis` (provided by the #2772 stated-axis resolver), `RotaryFlowParams`, and `AxisControl`.
- Require a ball-nose tool and at least two guide chains in this first slice; refuse empty, off-model, or single-chain inputs by name.
- Unwrap each chain into continuous cylindrical `(theta, v)` coordinates about `Axis` using `unwrap_near`, and align chain pairs by nearest `2 * pi` offset.
- Parameterize the pair by normalized arc length, compute developed width `(s = R_ref * theta, v)`, and choose pass count from `stepover` or `scallop_stepover(r, tolerance)`.
- Adaptively chord each interpolated flow curve within `ARC_FIT_TOL` / `tolerance`.
- Compute gouge-free radial ball centers `rho_ball(theta, v)` where `min_tri dist(center, tri) >= r` via `closest_pt_tri`, so steep helical flanks never gouge.
- Link passes radially on the retract cylinder (matching `rotary_links`) and emit tool tips via `retip` and `command_axis`.

Provenance: published 4-axis cylindrical unwrapping and iso-parametric flow-line CAM literature; no vendor material consulted.

Depends on #2772 for stated rotary axis resolution on helical models.

Done means: `crates/motion::multiaxis::rotary_flow` generates gouge-free, radially posed passes across multi-turn helical bands on a rotor mesh in `crates/motion/tests/` and refuses invalid or single-chain inputs by name.

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

body:
Part of #2574 (research answer 2).

The maintainer named the Solidcraft route in #2574: "Or use solidcrafts model with the joints defined in the solidcraft file. Either way i guess. if we go the solidcraft route a base model could be generated thru its MCP."

## Recommended in #2574
The contract is a file, not a live MCP call. Solidcraft (MIT OR Apache-2.0) exports an assembly with its joints as URDF (`export` tool, `docs/mcp.md` of tangency-labs/solidcraft). URDF is a public XML format (wiki.ros.org/urdf/XML): links, `revolute` and `prismatic` joints, `origin`, `axis`, `limit`, mesh references. `camcraft-sim` reads only the file and never needs Solidcraft at run time. Without a URDF, the model comes from the `.mch` (#2584, #2591).

## Open design points
1. The `.mch` key that names the URDF and maps each URDF joint to an axis letter.
2. The units and the root frame of the URDF against the machine frame and the `travel` of the `.mch`. Which file wins when the joint limits differ.
3. The mesh formats to read (STL and OBJ readers exist; GLB does not).
4. Refusals: a joint with no letter, a letter with no joint, a closed chain, a mesh that is not found.

## Done means
The design points have answers in comments, and the code sub-issue is filed with a `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` label. No hard dependency on Solidcraft is added.

body:
**Need (from a user, in our words):** Users keep one insert and many holders that accept it. Today each CamCraft tool is a separate whole, so the same insert is defined again in every holder. Wanted: a component library (inserts, holders, adapters, extensions), each with its own mounting coordinate system; holders state which inserts they accept; an assembly is built from components and stays linked, so a change to a component updates every assembly that uses it. Parametric tools remain and can serve as components.

**Reference:** ISO 13399 (cutting tool data representation: tool items, adaptive items, coordinate systems and connection interfaces). Clean-room: no competitor material.

**Related:** #1039 (lathe holder bodies placed by ISO 13399 coordinate systems), #1040 (tool bodies assembled from several vendor models), #2092 (a tool's library holder becomes a reference - the first step toward linked components).

**Open questions:**
1. Data model: which component kinds (insert, holder, adapter, extension, collet/chuck); which ISO 13399 coordinate systems and connection codes do we need?
2. Compatibility: how does a holder declare the inserts it takes (ISO insert shape, size, seat), and how do we refuse a wrong combination by name?
3. Linking: library references vs copies in a project; what happens when a linked component changes; project-file format and migration (relates to #2092).
4. Geometry: how the assembly's cutting edge, gauge line and body (for collision checks) are derived from the components' frames (relates to #1039, #1040).
5. Milling too? Indexable face mills and end mills use the same idea (body plus inserts).
6. UI and MCP: how users browse "holders that take this insert", and the commands needed (Everything Is a Command).

**Done means:** each question answered in a comment, a recorded design decision, and concrete sub-issues filed (each with P/effort/area), then this umbrella is closed.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer's collaborator (2026-11-16, after the v0.22.0 cut): "This should be smooth and quick. Pull all processing before the merge to main if possible. Velocity Velocity Velocity". These are proposals for the maintainer to decide. Nothing here changes a process file yet.

## What happened on 2026-11-16

| Phase | Time | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Merge stop to release branch | about 3.5 h | `main` did not compile (#2143, from #1753), a red test (#2137), a P1 found during the cut (#2152), and a P2 with two competing fix PRs (#2004: #2013 and #2141) |
| Release gate (`cut.yml`) | 1.6 h | the full release tier in one job on one runner |
| Merge, tag, `release.yml` | about 1 h | package builds on hosted runners |

Later the same day `main` went red two more times (#2198, #2244). Each time, two PRs that passed alone did not build or pass together (#2244: #2140 and #2077). The post-merge gate found each one, but only after the merge.

## Proposals

1. **Test the batch before the merge (a merge queue).** Before a merge batch, build a candidate: `main` plus every PR of the batch, merged in the `merge-plan` order. Run the batch tier on the candidate. Merge the batch only when the candidate is green. If it is red, remove the PR that breaks it and test again. The post-merge gate then only confirms. (mkinney's coordinator does this on its own machines from today, with the user's yes for each PR.)
2. **Check `main` on each new commit.** A fast compile check (clippy on all crates, `--all-targets`) and `cargo test -p xtask` take about 2 to 5 minutes with a warm cache. A failure names the merge within the hour. (mkinney's coordinator runs this hourly from today; it found #2244.)
3. **A cut-readiness verdict before "cut".** Before the merge stop: no open P1 or P2, no open release PR, the compile check and the batch tier green on that exact `main` sha, and the packaging dry run green. The result is one line: GO or NO-GO with the reasons.
4. **Reuse a green rehearsal at the cut.** Run the release tier nightly on `main`. If `release/vX.Y.Z` differs from a rehearsed sha only by release notes, `CHANGELOG.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` and the version bump, `cut.yml`'s gate stage accepts the rehearsal result (the same "gated tree is the tagged tree" check that the tag stage makes). Saves about 1.5 h.
5. **Split the release tier across runners.** The heavy lanes are independent. Run them as parallel jobs on the self-hosted runners (uma, m3 and others), then join the results. About 1.6 h becomes about 30 min when a full run is necessary.
6. **Measure `release.yml`.** Find the slowest job (probably macOS) and check the cache and split options.
7. **One fix for one P1/P2.** No second fix PR for an issue that already has one, and a known gap in a P1/P2 fix is fixed on the branch, not left as a note (the cause of #2152).

Target: a cut from GO to published release in about 1 hour, and `main` green between cuts.

## Open questions for the maintainer

- Accept 1 for all collaborator merges (the repository `merge-ready` skill would build and test the candidate before it merges)?
- Accept 4 and 5 for `cut.yml` (a process change, with a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump)?
- Which runner runs the nightly rehearsal (3 and 4)?

Done means: the maintainer decides each proposal on this issue, and each accepted one gets its own sub-issue.

body:
Create the pure-Rust crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`) beside `crates/post`.
It parses RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556) and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections (`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`) and a 1-based line map.

## Scope
- Depend only on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `thiserror` (no `boa_engine`, no `flecs_ecs`, no `camcraft-post` dependency).
- Record the new `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-geometry` crate edges in `docs/decisions/` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Accept dialect configuration and optional machine reference positions from the caller.
- Track modal groups: motion (`G0`, `G1`, `G2`, `G3`, `G80`), plane (`G17`, `G18`, `G19`), distance (`G90`, `G91`), arc center (`G90.1`, `G91.1`), feed mode (`G94`), units (`G20`, `G21`), length offset (`G43 H`, `G49`), work offsets (`G54`..`G59`), and cycle return (`G98`, `G99`).
- Parse `I`/`J`/`K` arcs and `R` radius arcs (`R > 0` minor arc, `R < 0` major arc) in XY, XZ, and YZ planes.
- Expand canned cycles (`G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G86`, `G89`) into explicit `cl::Move` chains (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs`).
- Handle `T`, `M6`, `S`, `M3`/`M4`/`M5`, `M0`/`M1`/`M2`/`M30`, `G4`, `G61`/`G64`, and `G53`/`G28`/`G30` when reference positions exist.
- Split sections on tool changes and record a 1-based source line number for every move.
- Refuse unknown words, missing unit mode, `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, and `A`/`B`/`C` words by name with the 1-based line number.
- Add a clean-room provenance comment to each module (`AGENTS.md`).

Done means: `camcraft-gcode` builds in the workspace with a `docs/decisions/` entry, parses 3-axis ISO programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections with a 1-based line map, and tests pin modal tracking, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs, canned cycles, unit scaling, and named line-numbered refusals.

body:
Asked on Discord (2026-11-16): "Are we going to do a trajectory simulation? Something like CAMotics?" The maintainer's collaborator wants it: "Yes open ticket, I would like that".

## What is missing

CamCraft simulates the toolpaths that it generates: stock removal, playback, and the tool, holder, fixture and machine-travel laws (#2181, #2193, #2194 improve the playback). It cannot open a G-code file and simulate it. Examples of files that users want to check:
- a program from a different CAM program;
- a hand-written or edited program;
- a CamCraft program that was edited after the post.

## Wanted

Open an `.nc` / `.tap` / `.gcode` file, select the machine (and with it the dialect), and simulate it with the existing stock simulation and verify laws: material removal, gouges against an optional model, collisions with the holder and fixtures, and travel limits. The result is the same view and the same findings as for CamCraft's own toolpaths.

## Open questions (research)

1. **Reader.** A G-code reader for each supported dialect (Fanuc, Haas, Tormach/LinuxCNC, grblHAL, Heidenhain conversational, Siemens, Mazak, Doosan, Sodick wire...). Which words are read: modal groups, G90/G91, G20/G21, arcs (I/J/K and R), planes G17/G18/G19, canned cycles (expanded to moves), tool changes (T/M6 and the tool length offset), work offsets, G28/G30/G53, subprograms and macros. What is refused by name.
2. **Tools.** How a file's tool numbers map to CamCraft tools: the machine's tool table, the document's tool library, or a prompt for each T number.
3. **Setup.** Stock, work offset and fixtures: taken from the open document, or entered with the file.
4. **Multi-axis.** 4th and 5th axis words, through the machine kinematics (the AC solver of #2056 in reverse).
5. **Units and errors.** A word that the reader does not understand gives a clear refusal with the line number, never a silent skip.
6. **Use of it.** A "compare" mode: post a CamCraft program, then read it back and simulate it, so that the post is checked end to end (a round-trip test for every built-in post).
7. **Where it lives.** A reader crate beside `camcraft-post` (domain only), with the open-file command and its MCP tool in `app`.

## Clean room

Specify the reader from public sources only: the G-code standards (RS-274/NGC, ISO 6983), the controls' published programming manuals, and our own post scripts. Do not read or adapt the code of CAMotics, LinuxCNC's interpreter or other G-code simulators. Do not use programs that Fusion 360 or HSMWorks generated as test input.

## Done means

The open questions are answered in comments on this issue, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #N"), linked back here. Then `needs-research` is dropped and this umbrella closes.

body:
Asked for by the user (2026-11-16, in chat), after comparing CamCraft with WAZER's WAM software, which "requires closed paths" and "does not do nesting":

> "By nesting, I mean here are parts, figure out how to optimally place them so I can minimize material waste"

> "I'd suspect the workflow would be to open the models (probably svg and dxf files, enter material info (dimensions, type, thickness), kerf and minimal space between cuts, and you'd press a button to have it do layout. WAM had options to do inside, on line, or outside line cutting. The cutting logic gets tricky because you have to do some cuts (like internal features) first"

## What is missing

CamCraft has no automatic nesting: there is no way to give it a set of 2D parts and a sheet and have it place the parts to waste as little material as possible. `#1447` (common-line cutting in a nest) assumes the parts are already placed.

## Wanted workflow (from the user)

1. Open the part drawings: SVG (`#1880`) and DXF (`#1452`, `#1865`), several files, with a quantity per part.
2. Enter the sheet: width x height, material type, thickness.
3. Enter the kerf and the minimum gap between cuts (and from the sheet edge).
4. Choose the cut side per part or per profile: inside, on the line, or outside the line.
5. Press one button: CamCraft lays out the parts on the sheet (and on more sheets if they do not fit), and shows the use of material.
6. The cut order follows from the layout: internal features (holes) before the part outline, small parts before the parts around them, and no part cut free while a later cut still needs it.

## Open questions (research)

1. **Algorithm.** True-shape nesting from published literature, for example no-fit polygons (Bennell and Oliveira, "The geometry of nesting problems: a tutorial", EJOR 2008; Burke et al., "Complete and robust no-fit polygon generation for the irregular stock cutting problem", EJOR 2007) with a bottom-left fill or a local-search placement order. Which method, what run time is acceptable, and is the result deterministic (same input, same layout)?
2. **Rotations and mirroring.** Free rotation, fixed steps (0/90/180/270 or 15 degrees), or locked (grain direction, a printed face)? Mirroring allowed?
3. **Spacing.** How the kerf, the minimum gap, leads and pierce points enter the spacing (offset each part by half the kerf plus half the gap before nesting?). The sheet edge margin, and holes or scrap areas already in the sheet (a remnant).
4. **Parts in holes.** May a small part be placed inside a large part's hole?
5. **Document model.** Is a nest a new entity (sheet + placed part instances) with undoable commands (`CreateNest`, `EditNest`, `RunNesting`) and their MCP tools (AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command" and "Commands ship with an MCP tool")? How does it relate to setups and stock?
6. **Cut order.** Holes before outlines; inside-out for parts inside holes; the "no part drops before its remaining cuts" rule shared with `#1447`; which machine kinds (waterjet, plasma, laser, router sheet jobs).
7. **Cut side.** Inside / on / outside the line per profile, mapped onto the 2D profile and waterjet operations (`#1883`), with open paths handled where the operation allows (WAM cannot cut open paths).
8. **Output.** Material use (percent), the waste outline, and a sheet count.

## Clean room

Specify from published literature and our own design notes only. Do not read or adapt nesting code or other CAM programs' internals (Fusion, HSMWorks, WAM's JavaScript, SVGnest, Deepnest and the like are not sources). The user's own WAM projects (G-code beside `.wzr` files, which the user cleared for reading) may be used only to compare CamCraft's output on the same parts.

## Done means

The open questions are answered in comments on this issue, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #N"), linked back here; then `needs-research` is dropped and this umbrella closes.

Related: `#1447` (common-line cutting in a nest), `#1883` (waterjet profile operation), `#1886` (WAZER machines and post), `#1880` (SVG import), `#1452` (DXF import), `#1861` (outer vs hole chaining).

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15. His words: "we want a CPS editor in the Application. Where we can start from scratch of a "blank template", and pick like "a standard 2D operation" and it would generate some Gcode that reprsents the output of that operation, using the editors temporary .cps so a blank would do nothing right, but as we stack in functionality the g-code file would output correctly..  And the editor should live in its own panel so we can effectivly close everything else if we need. Thus giving more room for picking "common snippets" from a library in the editor to modify."

This issue is research. It gets no code, no branch and no PR. The research answers the questions below in comments and files the sub-issues.

## The idea

- The application has an editor for post scripts (`.cps`).
- The user starts from a blank template. A blank template posts nothing.
- The user selects a sample program, for example a standard 2D operation. The editor runs the temporary script on that sample and shows the G-code.
- When the user adds a function to the script, the preview shows the new output.
- The editor has a library of common snippets. The user inserts a snippet and changes it.
- The editor is a panel of its own. The user can close all other panels to give it the room.

## Questions for the research

1. What is the smallest script that the post engine (`camcraft-post`) accepts, and what does it post? Define the blank template.
2. Which sample programs does the editor offer? Recorded `.cl` files (for example from `crates/app/tests/golden/`) need no generator and no open project. Is "the operations of the open project" a second source?
3. How does the preview run: on each edit with a delay, or on a command? What is the time limit of one run, and how does the editor stop a script that does not end?
4. How does the editor show a script error: the line, the message, and the last good output?
5. Which snippets are in the first library (program start and end, tool change, spindle and coolant, linear and arc moves, canned cycles, work offset, sequence numbers)? Where are they stored, and can a user add one?
6. Which text editor widget does egui give us (syntax colours, line numbers, undo in the text, find)? Does a dependency come with it? A new dependency needs the maintainer's decision.
7. Where does a saved script go (a user directory, not `assets/posts/`), and how does the Machines and Posts page find it?
8. Which editor actions are commands with undo, and which are text-edit state of the widget only? Which MCP tools does the editor need?
9. How does the panel fit the panel layout (#2002 gives tools their own panels)?
10. Relation to #2049 (post options in the Post dialog): the editor must show and edit the declared options of the script too.

## Rules that apply

- Clean-room: the snippets and the template are written from our own scripts and from public G-code standards. Do not copy text or code of the post processors of other products.
- A script from the editor goes through the same verification gate and the same refusals as a shipped script. The preview never writes a program file that a machine can run without the normal post step.
- The preview output is marked as a preview.

## Done means (for this research issue)

- Each question has an answer in a comment, with the facts from the code.
- The sub-issues are filed with their `P*`, `effort:*` and `area:*` labels and are named here.
- Then this issue is closed.

body:
Add a dedicated `WaterjetProfile` 2D through-cut operation by extracting shared sheet-cutting helpers from `motion::plasma` and `motion::wire_edm`.

Depends on #1881 and #1882.

## Scope

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/`):**
  - Extract pure contour nesting (`nest.rs`), `Region::offset` kerf rings (`ring.rs`), `kerf_law` / `cover_law` (`laws.rs`), open-contour left/right offsets (`wire_edm/open.rs`), and flat tab splitting (`wire_edm/tabs.rs`) into shared helpers.
  - Reuse those helpers across `plasma`, `wire_edm`, and `waterjet` without duplicating geometry logic.
  - Add straight and arc lead-in/lead-out support on open chains created by tab gaps (`crates/motion/src/plasma/emit.rs` currently cuts open chains on centerline with no leads).
- **Waterjet profile generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`):**
  - Cut inner holes before enclosing outer contours.
  - Offset geometry by half-kerf (outside, inside, or left/right open chains) with optional control compensation (`G41`/`G42`) when supported.
  - Cut flat tabs as uncut gaps (`count`, `width`, `at`) that turn closed loops into open chains with safe pierce leads outside the part edge.
  - Handle tight holes by shortening leads to clear opposite kerf or center-piercing when needed, without plasma THC assumptions.
  - Apply configurable arc linearization (`Move::chords(tol)`) when enabled.
- **App, commands, persistence, and UI (`crates/app`, `crates/ui`):**
  - Register `OpType::WaterjetProfile`, `Family::Waterjet`, and `Section::Waterjet` in `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`.
  - Add undoable commands, `.camproj` serialization DTO, UI ribbon mode/icon/page (kerf side, leads, tabs, pierce and abrasive dwell, cut-data selection, without plasma height/THC fields).

**Done means:** `WaterjetProfile` generates inner-first kerf-offset paths with leads on closed contours and tabbed open chains, round-trips in `.camproj` via undoable commands, shows in the UI on `Kind::Waterjet` machines, and matches golden CL output for a tabbed plate with holes.

Part of #1525

body:
The maintainer asked for this issue in chat on 2026-11-15: "Issue; enhancement; Operation; 3D-Debur - research online, find papers on it usingg perplexity, document it as an issue."

This issue records the research. It also lists the work that the 3D Deburr operation needs to become a full edge-break operation. An agent filed it for the maintainer.

## What we have today

The Deburr operation exists (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/deburr.rs`, `OpParams::Deburr`). It does this:

- It finds the edges automatically: convex creases and open rims of the mesh.
- It uses a cone tool (chamfer mill) with a vertical tool axis.
- It has one authored number, `width`. The tip depth follows: `drop = width / tan(half-angle)`.
- It does not cut steep edges. It skips an edge that climbs faster than the cone flank and writes a note (#303).
- It clips the ride to the `top_z` / `bottom_z` window.

## What is missing

1. The user cannot select edges. The user cannot exclude edges.
2. There is no filter for the edge angle. There is no filter for holes.
3. Only the cone tool works. A ball mill and a lollipop mill do not work. Tool kinds are also a subject of #895 and #896.
4. Steep and vertical edges get no edge break.
5. The break has one shape only. There is no constant-depth mode, no large chamfer in more than one pass, and no rounded edge.
6. The tool axis is always vertical. Edges under an overhang, and edges on the side of the part, are out of reach.
7. There is no setting that says what to do with a part of an edge that the tool cannot reach.

## Research

### Behaviour of a deburr strategy in other CAM systems (public documentation, behaviour only)

Sources: the Autodesk Fusion help page "Generate a Deburr toolpath" (https://help.autodesk.com/view/fusion360/ENU/?contextId=MFG-MULTI-AXIS-DEBURR), the Autodesk blog (https://www.autodesk.com/products/fusion-360/blog/deburring-autodesk-fusion-360-tutorial/) and the Cimatron help page (https://help.cimatron.com/en/2026/english/tool_path_calculation/deburring/deburring_overview.htm). No vendor text, parameter name or asset is copied here.

- The operation follows the external edges of the part and makes a chamfer or a rounded edge.
- The system finds the edges automatically, or the user selects them. The user can exclude edges.
- A minimum edge angle removes edges that are almost tangent.
- The user can exclude circular holes, with a diameter range.
- The edge break has a constant width or a constant depth. A large chamfer and a rounded edge need more than one pass.
- Ball, lollipop, flat, chamfer, tapered and spot-drill tools are permitted in Fusion. Cimatron permits ball and lollipop tools only.
- The contact point can be a fixed point along the flute.
- The operation has a 3-axis, a 4-axis and a 5-axis mode. The 3-axis mode cuts only the edges that the tool can reach from above, and it can exclude vertical edges.
- A setting controls the areas that the tool cannot reach.
- The system checks the holder for collisions. In a multi-axis mode it changes the tilt when it finds a collision.

### Papers and standards

| Subject | Source |
|---|---|
| Burr definition, burr types, edge measure, removal methods (review) | Aurich, Dornfeld, Arrazola, Franke, Leitz, Min: "Burrs - Analysis, control and removal", CIRP Annals 58(2), 519-542, 2009. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cirp.2009.09.004 (open copy: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/1sc2k1b8) |
| Edge states on a drawing: burr, sharp edge, undercut; one value "edge measure a" | ISO 13715, edges of undefined shape (editions 2000 and later). Licensed document: use the summary in the CIRP review. |
| Conference papers on burr control and removal | Aurich, Dornfeld (eds.): "Burrs - Analysis, Control and Removal", Springer, 2010. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-00568-8 |
| 3-axis ball-end path along a hole intersection curve, constant chamfer | Abele, Schützer, Güth, Meinhard: "Deburring of cross-drilled holes with ball-end cutters - modeling the tool path", Production Engineering 12, 25-33, 2018. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11740-017-0781-0 |
| Numerical 3-axis ball-end path on complex intersections, maximum ball diameter, collision avoidance | Schützer, Abele, Meinhard et al.: "Deburring of complex-shaped drilling intersections: a numerical method for modelling the tool path", Int J Adv Manuf Technol 102, 67-79, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-018-3205-1 |

| Deburr paths from CAD edges: group the edges, make a tool pose for each edge, add approach and depart points | NIST: "CAD Directed Robotic Deburring" (https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=820241) and "An Advanced Deburring and Chamfering System" (https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=820281) |
| Position and orientation planning, deburr in layers | "A Robotic Deburring Methodology for Tool Path Planning and Process Parameter Control of a Five-Degree-of-Freedom Robot Manipulator", Applied Sciences 9(10), 2033, 2019. https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/9/10/2033 |
| Tool trajectory from a 3D scan (mesh input, no B-rep) | Onstein, Bjerkeng, Martinsen: "Automated Tool Trajectory Generation for Robotized Deburring of Cast Parts Based on 3D Scans", Procedia CIRP 118, 507-512, 2023. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.procir.2023.06.087 |
| Lead angle and edge curvature change the chamfer width on a 5-axis machine | "Analysis of the Deburring Efficiency of EN-AW 7075 Aluminum Alloy ...", Materials 17(24), 6267, 2024. https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1944/17/24/6267 |

Limits of this research:

- One long research request timed out, and one request got a rate-limit error. The table comes from search results and abstracts.
- Nobody has read the full text of the papers behind a paywall. The design step must read a paper before it uses a formula from it.
- The details of other CAM systems (hyperMILL, Mastercam, SolidCAM) are not verified and are not used here.
- No source confirmed typical drawing values for an edge break.

### Geometry (our derivation from elementary geometry; the design step must check it against the papers)

Symbols: `E` is a point on a convex edge. `n1` and `n2` are the outward unit normals of the two faces. `b = (n1 + n2) / |n1 + n2|` is the bisector that points out of the material. `θ` is the angle of the material wedge. The angle between the normals is `π - θ`.

- **Edge filter.** An edge is a candidate when it is convex and the angle between the normals is not less than the minimum edge angle. The current crease test already finds convex pairs.
- **Symmetric chamfer.** A chamfer with setback `s` on each face has the width `w = 2·s·sin(θ/2)`. Its plane is perpendicular to `b`. The plane is at the depth `d = s·cos(θ/2)` below `E`.
- **Ball of radius R, centre on the bisector.** The centre is `C = E + h·b` with `h = -s·cos(θ/2) + sqrt(R² - s²·sin²(θ/2))`. The ball then cuts each face at the setback `s`. The condition is `R >= w/2`. The ball makes a concave break, not a flat chamfer. The ball centre does not depend on the tool axis, thus the same law is correct for the 3-axis mode and the multi-axis modes. For a lollipop tool, the axis must also keep the neck clear.
- **Cone tool with half-angle α.** The flank makes a flat symmetric chamfer only when the angle between the tool axis and `b` is `90° - α`. With a vertical axis, the break is symmetric only on some edges. The current ride accepts this and defines `width` in the horizontal plane of the edge.
- **Reach, 3-axis.** A ball position is legal only if the ball, the shank and the holder do not touch other faces. The existing envelope check (`verify`, `Mode::Envelope`) is the judge.

## Proposed slices (each one becomes a sub-issue)

1. Edge set: manual selection and exclusion of edges, a minimum edge angle, and a hole filter with a diameter range. Each one needs a command, a project file field, an MCP tool and a UI control.
2. Ball and lollipop tools in the 3-axis mode, with the ball-centre law above. A lollipop tool reaches a steep or vertical edge from the side.
3. Break shape: constant width or constant depth, and a larger chamfer or a rounded edge in more than one pass.
4. A setting for a part of an edge that the tool cannot reach: skip it with a note, or refuse the operation by name.
5. Multi-axis mode (4-axis and 5-axis): the tool axis tilts to reach edges, with a collision check of the holder.
6. Simulation: the edge-break records (#303, #529) must accept the new break shapes, so that the gouge check does not refuse an intended break.

Each strategy choice is a user parameter with a default. No choice is fixed in the code.

## Open questions (reason for `needs-research`)

- Does manual edge selection select mesh edge chains, or the B-rep edges of the solid model when the import has them?
- Which definition of "width" is the one setting for all tools: the chamfer width `w`, or the setback `s`?
- Is the multi-axis mode a mode of this operation, or a different operation in the multi-axis family?
- What are the default minimum edge angle and the default width?

## Safety

This work changes toolpath geometry and the gouge check, thus the safety floor applies to each sub-issue (`effort:high` or more). A break that the tool cannot make safely must be refused or skipped with a note. It must never be cut wrong.

Done means: the open questions have answers in comments, the sub-issues are filed with "Part of" this issue, and this issue is closed with a comment that names them.
