body:
Part of #1152 (and #543). Found while working #1152.

**What happens:** the size law (`sinker_undersize::judge`) judges a body electrode on the X and Y extents of its outline. An inward offset moves a sharp corner that is not square to the axes further than the undersize. For such a cavity (a diamond, a rotated rectangle) the extents that the spark gap reaches are short of the cavity's extents. A finish pass is then refused: "sinker finish leaves the cavity under size". A rough pass and a single pass are generated.

The refusal is true to the model: a round gap does not reach a sharp corner. But the user cannot make a finish pass of such a cavity, and the stock sim judges the same burn clean within its tolerance.

**What is wanted:** the size law compares the electrode's outline with the cavity's outline, not their extents. The Sinker Burn then states the cavity's outline (today it states `cavity_x` and `cavity_y` only). A finish is refused only when a wall is left under size by more than the slack.

**Evidence:** `crates/motion/src/sinker_undersize.rs` (the module head and `Undersize::outline`), `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_body.rs` (`a_cavity_turned_from_the_axes_is_judged_on_its_outlines_extents`), `docs/decisions/1152-electrode-body.md`.

**Done means:** a finish pass of a diamond pocket with the electrode that `electrode_from_faces` makes for its finish condition is generated, and the program verdict judges it clean. An electrode that is too large for the cavity is still refused by name. The new parameter has its MCP schema entry.

body:
**The request (the user, 2026-11-14):** "create an ai chat window in CamCraft that would interact with ai thru mcp or whatever appropriate. Make sure that we help those agents with appropriate skill stuff for various ai tools like Claude, codex, Gemini, unsloth, ollama, etc."

This is a research umbrella (`needs-research`). It answers the open questions below in comments. Then it files the concrete sub-issues and closes. No code goes on this issue.

## What exists today

- `camcraft-cli mcp` is an MCP server on stdio. An agent drives one headless document.
- The app can start with `--mcp-port`, and `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` bridges an external agent to the open window. The agent then drives the live document.
- The skill `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/` documents the tools for Claude Code.
- Every MCP tool calls the same undoable commands as the GUI (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Goal

1. **In-app chat panel.** A dock panel in CamCraft where the user types a request, for example "add a 2D pocket on the selected face with T3". An AI model answers and acts through the same MCP tool set. The panel shows each tool call and its result.
2. **Provider choice.** The user picks the model provider and the model:
   - **Cloud:** Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT/Codex models), Google (Gemini).
   - **Local:** Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp server (most local servers have an OpenAI-compatible API).
3. **External agents.** Each external agent tool gets one documented way to drive the open app (`--mcp-port` plus `mcp --connect`), and a skill or instruction file in its own format:
   - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/` (exists; keep it current);
   - Codex CLI: AGENTS.md section or `.codex/` instructions;
   - Gemini / Antigravity CLI: `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/skills/`;
   - local models through Ollama or Unsloth: a short system prompt plus the tool list.

## Open questions (answer each in a comment)

1. **Panel architecture.** In-process, where the app calls the provider API and maps the MCP tools to the provider's tool-calling format? Or a separate process that speaks MCP to the app? What keeps the UI thread free (async, cancel)?
2. **One tool schema for all providers.** Map the MCP tool schemas to the Anthropic Messages tool format, the OpenAI tools format, and Gemini function declarations. Which local models do tool calling well enough? What is the fallback for a model without tool calling?
3. **Safety.**
   - Every action goes through the undoable commands.
   - The chat never posts G-code, never writes a file, and never changes a machine without a confirmation in the panel.
   - Group one chat turn as one undo step, or one step per command?
   - How does the panel show what changed?
4. **Keys and privacy.**
   - Where do API keys live (the OS keychain)?
   - What is sent to a cloud model (the project data, the model geometry)?
   - How does an offline-only setting work (local models only)?
5. **Context size.** How does a large project (many operations, big meshes) fit a model's context window? Summaries, on-demand tool reads?
6. **Skills per tool.** One source of truth for the tool docs (generated from the MCP tool list?) with per-tool wrappers, so the docs never drift from the shipped tools.
7. **Tests.** Test the panel and the tool mapping without network access (a scripted fake provider).
8. **Clean room.** Only public API documentation of each provider and the MCP specification. No code or prompts copied from other CAM products.

## Sub-issues to file (when the research is done)

- The chat panel: UI, history, tool-call display, cancel, confirmation prompts.
- The provider adapters: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible local (Ollama, Unsloth, LM Studio, llama.cpp).
- The tool-schema mapping, generated from the MCP tool list.
- Keys and privacy settings, plus the offline mode.
- Skill and instruction files for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity and local models, generated from one source.
- Docs (REQUIRED): "Use AI with CamCraft": setup and worked examples for every provider (Claude, OpenAI/Codex, Gemini, Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and every external agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini/Antigravity CLI, headless). See the comment that adds docs to the scope.

**Done means:** every open question has an answered comment, every sub-issue is filed with "Part of #this", and this umbrella is closed.

title: Operations: pre-drilled holes as entry positions (plunge to full depth instead of helix)

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "Another issue is setting pre drilled holes as starting points for some operations so we can dive down and do properly full depth cuts instead of trying to helix down little bit at a time..."

What is missing: a pocket or adaptive operation in closed material always works its own way down (helix or ramp), a little at a time. The usual shop method, drilling a start hole first and plunging the end mill down it to full depth, cannot be set up: the operation does not know a hole is there.

Wanted: on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Slot and the 3D roughing operations, an "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group:
- Pick one or more points or existing drilled holes (a drilling operation earlier in the setup, a hole in the model, or a typed point with a diameter and depth).
- At such a position the tool goes straight down the hole at the plunge/rapid-in-clearance feed to the cutting depth and starts the full-depth cut from there, with no helix or ramp. Depth passes may then be full depth (the user's stepdown still rules).
- Regions with no entry position keep the helix or ramp, or are refused if the user chose "pre-drilled only".

Safety (this is a plunge into what the program believes is air):
- The hole must really be there when the operation runs: its source is an earlier operation in the same setup (or carried stock from a previous setup), checked against the stock simulation; a typed point with no drilling behind it is allowed only with the user's explicit "the hole exists" choice, shown in the operation summary and the setup sheet.
- The hole must be at least as wide as the tool plus a clearance and at least as deep as the plunge; otherwise refused by name with the numbers. A hole with a drill-point cone is counted only to its full-diameter depth.
- The entry must lie inside the region to cut, and the first sideways move starts from the hole wall, not from solid.
- The rapid-in-stock and gouge checks stay on: a plunge down a hole that the simulation does not show is refused at the post like any other.

Related: the companion issue on user-set start and exit points (filed with this one); tool kinds for drills are issue 897.

Done means: a closed pocket with a drilled start hole from an earlier operation plunges down the hole and cuts at full depth with no helix (golden CL, simulation clean); a hole too small or too shallow is refused by name in tests; a typed position without a drilling operation is refused unless the explicit choice is set; undo and redo; MCP parameters; the structural UI test covers the group.

body:
Maintainer direction (2026-11-11): "We should aim for a high cohesion low coupling thru out our codebase as we are built crates and tests. And every gate is very costly."

Where the cost comes from today (measured 2026-11-11 on main 0e36fd14):

| Crate | Source lines | Test files (one binary each) | Depends on (workspace) |
|---|---|---|---|
| app | 72,122 | 267 | cl, geometry, motion, post, sim, tools |
| ui | 57,060 | 14 | app |
| motion | 46,643 | 65 | cl, geometry, sim, tools |
| sim | 23,444 | 50 | cl, geometry, tools |
| post | 6,181 | 5 | cl, geometry |
| geometry | 5,539 | 4 | - |
| tools | 4,306 | 1 | - |
| cl | 3,723 | 1 | - |
| kernel | 1,185 | 5 | - |

- `app` is the hub: it depends on every domain crate, so almost any change rebuilds it, and each of its 267 test files links the whole crate into its own binary.
- Tests of one domain's behaviour live in `app` (post dialect tests such as `fanuc_post`, `tormach_post`, `heidenhain_*` sit in `crates/app/tests/` while `crates/post/tests/` has 5 files), so a post-only change still builds and links `app`.
- A geometry / cl / Cargo change falls back to the batch tier.
- Each worktree's `target/` is 25-56 GB; five builds at once took the disk from 166 GB to 13 GB free on 2026-11-11.

Open questions to answer here (research, no code):
1. Fan-out: for a change in each crate, which crates and how many test binaries rebuild and relink, and how long does it take (cold and warm, with #913's cache)? One table.
2. Test placement: which `crates/app/tests/*` files test behaviour owned by post, sim, motion, cl, tools or geometry and could move to that crate with a small fixture seam instead of the whole app? Count per target crate.
3. Test binaries: what does folding a crate's test files into a few binaries (one per gate-map group) save in link time and disk, and what does it cost (`gate test <name>` selection, parallel runs, the quick tier's changed-test picking in `xtask/src/plan.rs`)?
4. Coupling: which `app` modules could become their own crate (the M4.1 seams still inside `app`: operation, project, commands, mcp, machine), and which dependencies between domain crates could be cut or inverted (motion -> sim; the new post -> tools from PR #880)?
5. Rules: which of this becomes law in AGENTS.md "Code shape" and a reviewer check (e.g. a test lives in the crate that owns the behaviour; a new dependency between workspace crates needs a decision entry; no new test file in `app` for behaviour another crate owns)?

Then file the concrete sub-issues (each with P*, effort, area, "Done means", "Part of #<this>"), ordered by gate minutes saved per unit of work, and close this umbrella.

Related: #900 / PR #913 (compile cache and lighter dev profile), #27 (kernel seam).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
